title: The tenses on one line
subtitle: English tenses on a timeline
review: Written by Claude in the format of the French tense pages. Check the examples and the level.
intro: Move along the line from the past to the future. Each point is a tense: see when it is used, how it is made, and what one verb looks like in it. A bar shows a tense that lasts: an action in progress, or a past that reaches now.

tenses.name: past perfect
tenses.hint: The past of the past: it was already over before another past moment.
tenses.use: An action that happened before another action in the past.

examples.fr: When we arrived, the film **had started**.
I was tired because I **had not slept** well.
He said he **had lost** his bag.

tenses.name: past continuous
tenses.hint: A stretch of the past, not a point: the action was going on.
tenses.use: An action in progress at a moment in the past, and the background of a story.

examples.fr: At eight o'clock I **was eating** breakfast.
The sun **was shining** and the birds **were singing**.

tenses.name: past simple
tenses.hint: A finished point in the past. We know when.
tenses.use: Finished actions, and stories: one thing after another.
tenses.structure: verb + **-ed**, or an irregular form: go → **went**

examples.fr: She **bought** a new bag last week.

tenses.name: present perfect
tenses.hint: A bridge from the past to now: it happened before, and it still matters.
tenses.use: Experience, a result you can see now, and things that started in the past and are still true.

examples.fr: We **have lived** here for ten years.

tenses.name: present simple
tenses.hint: Now, in the widest sense: what is always or usually true.
tenses.use: Habits, facts, and what you like, know and want.
tenses.structure: verb, and verb + **-s** for he / she / it

examples.fr: I **get up** at six every day.

tenses.name: present continuous
tenses.hint: This very moment: it has started and it is not finished.
tenses.use: What is happening now or around now, and fixed plans.

tenses.name: be going to
tenses.hint: The future grows out of now: you have a plan, or you can see it coming.
tenses.use: Plans you already have, and things you can see are about to happen.

examples.fr: I **am going to visit** my uncle tomorrow.
Look at those clouds. It **is going to rain**.

tenses.name: will
tenses.hint: The open future: decisions made now, promises, and what you think will happen.
tenses.use: Decisions at the moment of speaking, promises, offers, and what you think about the future.

examples.fr: I'm thirsty. I **will get** some water.
